prediction.likelyOutcome: Caton most likely wins the core Section 9(a) trigger question — the fifth amendment's recital that the Section 1(b) conditions 'would not be satisfied' if the option were exercised largely defeats the Trust's 'never exercised, so nothing ripened' defense — and recovers the $314,000 in option consideration on partial summary judgment. The $128,885.50 expense claim is the weak flank: proved only by deposition testimony, arguably incurred by Management Services Company rather than by Caton, and arguably outside Section 2(b) 'diligence,' so expect it to survive to trial and be substantially discounted or cut. Probability-weighted net recovery lands in the low-to-mid $200,000s against a $442,885.50 demand.

outcome.description: The circuit court granted Caton summary judgment on a futility theory and awarded him $442,885.50 in damages (the full amount of his demand) plus $96,329.00 in attorneys' fees. The Court of Appeals of Virginia affirmed that the agreement required Caton to exercise the option, but reversed the summary judgment award of damages and fees because futility was not established as a matter of law, and remanded for further proceedings.
outcome.finalNote: Summary judgment reversed and remanded; no final figure yet.
